life.title: Personal privacy beyond apps
life.lead: The best VPN can't fix oversharing, weak locks, or a camera pointed at your desk. Privacy is a lifestyle system.

1.title: Social & identity
1.1: Audit public profiles — strip DOB, home city, workplace, family photos.
1.2: Use different usernames per context; stop recycling one handle everywhere.
1.3: Turn off face recognition and contact syncing in social apps.
1.4: Think before you post location in real time (wait until you've left).
1.5: Create separate email aliases for shopping, newsletters, and banking.

2.title: Home & physical
2.1: Cover laptop cameras; prefer mics you can mute in hardware.
2.2: Lock screens aggressively; enable full-disk encryption everywhere.
2.3: Shred or destroy documents with ID numbers — don't just recycle.
2.4: Question smart speakers in private rooms; segment IoT on guest Wi‑Fi.
2.5: Know who has physical access to your devices when you travel.

3.title: Money & shopping
3.1: Use privacy-friendly payment options where legal and practical.
3.2: Avoid store loyalty cards tied to your real identity when possible.
3.3: Don't photograph credit cards or IDs into cloud camera rolls.
3.4: Opt out of data brokers (varies by country — do annual sweeps).
3.5: Keep financial 2FA on hardware keys or authenticator apps, never SMS alone.

4.title: Communication habits
4.1: Default to Signal for anything you wouldn't put on a postcard.
4.2: Disappearing messages for ephemeral plans; screenshots still exist.
4.3: Verify safety numbers for high-stakes contacts.
4.4: Don't discuss secrets on employer devices or workplace chat.
4.5: Assume group chats expand your threat surface with every new member.

android.title: Android hardening checklist
android.note: GrapheneOS users: sandboxed Google Play is optional — only if you truly need it.
android.1: Prefer a modern Pixel + GrapheneOS if you can. Otherwise keep stock OS updated.
android.2: Install apps from trusted sources — Play Store carefully, or F-Droid for FOSS.
android.3: Permission diet: deny location, mic, camera, contacts unless required. Use only while using.
android.4: Disable ad ID / ads personalization and reset advertising IDs.
android.5: Turn off unnecessary sensors and connectivity: Bluetooth, NFC, precise location when idle.
android.6: Use a DNS blocker (Private DNS / RethinkDNS / NextDNS) to cut tracker domains.
android.7: Lock screen: strong PIN/passphrase, biometrics OK as convenience with PIN fallback.
android.8: Backup plan: encrypted backups you control — not only Google One defaults.
android.9: Work profile / secondary user to isolate sketchy apps from your main life.
android.10: Avoid sideloading APKs from random sites — supply-chain malware is common.

ios.title: iOS hardening checklist
ios.note: iOS is closed-source — compensate with strong Apple ID security and minimal app surface.
ios.1: Update iOS promptly — Apple's sandbox is strong; unpatched is not.
ios.2: Enable Lockdown Mode if you face targeted attacks (extreme but effective).
ios.3: Privacy and Security: review every permission; reset tracking; disable unused Bluetooth sharing.
ios.4: Apple ID hygiene: strong unique password, hardware key or passkeys, Hide My Email for sign-ins.
ios.5: iCloud: know what's syncing. Advanced Data Protection strengthens E2EE for more categories.
ios.6: Limit Analytics and Improvements and personalized ads.
ios.7: Safari: enable Fraudulent Website Warning; consider Firefox Focus or Brave for extra blocking.
ios.8: App Tracking Transparency: deny by default. Still assume apps track within their walls.
ios.9: USB accessories / Stolen Device Protection for physical threat models.
ios.10: Avoid shady configuration profiles and enterprise MDMs you don't understand.

macos.2: Review Privacy and Security permissions per app regularly.
macos.3: iCloud: enable Advanced Data Protection if suitable for your recovery setup.
macos.4: Prefer App Store or verified developers; Gatekeeper stays on.
macos.5: Limit Continuity features that broadcast presence if threat model requires it.
macos.6: Use Firefox/Brave; containerize work vs personal browsing.
macos.7: Lock screen hot corners + short idle timeout.

linux.3: Flatpak + Flathub with care; prefer distro packages for system tools.

principles.title: Privacy principles that never go out of date

p1.title: Threat model first
p1.body: Protect against the risks you actually face — not a movie villain. Different jobs need different stacks.

p2.title: Minimize data
p2.body: You can't leak what you never collect. Share less, keep less, delete what you don't need.

p3.title: Defense in depth
p3.body: One tool fails. Layer passwords, 2FA, encryption, updates, and good habits.

p4.title: Prefer open and audited
p4.body: Open source isn't magic, but secrecy is a worse bet for security-critical software.

p5.title: Usability wins
p5.body: The private tool you abandon is worse than the good-enough tool you use daily.

p6.title: Assume breach
p6.body: Plan recovery: backups, key escrow you control, and accounts you can still reclaim.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: Do I need a VPN every day?
faq.a1: Not always. A VPN hides your traffic from local networks and your ISP, and can reduce location-based tracking — but it does not make you anonymous, and a bad VPN is worse than none. Use a reputable no-logs provider on hostile networks; combine with HTTPS, good browsers, and account hygiene.
faq.q2: Is Signal really private if it needs my phone number?
faq.a2: Signal encrypts message content excellently. Your number is an identifier for discovery — a tradeoff for usability. If that matters for your threat model, look at Session or similar. For most people, Signal is still the best everyone-will-actually-use-it choice.
faq.a3: A password manager + unique passwords + authenticator 2FA on email. Most account takeovers are reused passwords and SIM swaps, not nation-state zero-days.
faq.a4: If you can, it helps a lot. If you can't, lock down profiles, strip personal data, stop real-time location posts, and use a browser container so trackers don't follow you across the whole web.
faq.a5: No analytics, no cookies for advertising, no third-party trackers for ads. Checklist progress stays in your browser's local storage only. Verify with your own blocker if you like — that's the point.
faq.a6: Read project docs for tools you adopt (Signal, Bitwarden, GrapheneOS, Mullvad). Community resources like privacyguides.org and official security whitepapers beat random top-10 VPN lists.
faq.q7: Is PrivGuide just marketing for PrivyDeck and PrivBeacon?
faq.a7: No. The guide is owned by the same company, which we disclose upfront. Independent tools are listed first; Ours are labeled. We publish conflicts and methodology on the Trust page. If a listing feels unfair, open a GitHub issue.
faq.q8: Do you get paid when I click an app link?
faq.a8: No. PrivGuide does not use affiliate links. Tips via crypto donations are optional and do not buy rankings.

methodology.1: Recommendations are practical, not maximalist. Usability counts: a private tool you abandon is worse than a good-enough tool you use daily.
methodology.2: We review listings on a rolling schedule. Each card shows a last-reviewed date. Criteria below apply to first-party and third-party tools alike.

criteria.1: Threat-model fit — clear who it protects against, and who it does not.
criteria.2: Security posture — encryption, open source or auditable claims, update cadence, history of incidents.
criteria.3: Privacy business model — how the vendor makes money; avoid predatory free tiers that sell attention.
criteria.4: Jurisdiction & governance — where the org is based and what legal pressure looks like.
criteria.5: Usability — will non-experts actually switch and stick with it?
criteria.6: Official distribution — we link only to official sites or well-known trusted repos (e.g. project GitHub).

transparency.1: PrivGuide is a static site. There is no account system and no advertising.

firefox.desc: Beste balanse av brukervennlighet og kontroll. Kombiner med PrivyDeck og/eller uBlock Origin, containere og streng sporingsbeskyttelse.

brave.desc: Chromium-basert med innebygd annonse-/sporingsblokkering og private vinduer med Tor-valg.
brave.why: du vil ha Chrome-lignende UX med bedre standarder.

tor.desc: Ruter trafikk gjennom Tor-nettverket. Essensielt for høyrisiko-research og sensur-omgåelse. Ikke for daglig innlogging.
tor.why: trusselmodellen trenger anonymitet, ikke bare personvern.

mullvad_browser.desc: Tor Browser-teknologi uten Tor-nettverket — personvernherdet Firefox for mindre fingerprinting.

librewolf.desc: Herdet Firefox-fork med telemetri fjernet og sterke anti-fingerprinting-standarder ferdig satt. Utmerket daglig nettleser.
librewolf.why: du vil ha Firefox-personvern uten å håndtune about:config.

mullvad.desc: Anonyme kontoer (ingen e-post), kontant/krypto-betaling, revidert, no-logs-rykte.
mullvad.why: du bryr deg mer om personvern enn raskest streaming.

protonvpn.desc: Solid gratisnivå, åpne apper, Secure Core og Proton-økosystem. Bra for nybegynnere.

ivpn.desc: Transparent personvernfirma, ingen e-postregistrering, sterke anti-sporingsfunksjoner.
ivpn.why: du vil ha Mullvad-lignende verdier med flere funksjoner.

bitwarden.desc: Åpen kildekode, revidert, gratis for enkeltpersoner. Self-host med Vaultwarden for full kontroll.
bitwarden.why: du fortsatt gjenbruker passord (start her i dag).

keepassxc.desc: Lokal-først passorddatabase. Du styrer filen, backup og synk. Null skyavhengighet.
keepassxc.why: du ikke vil ha tredjeparts vault-sky.

protonpass.desc: Integrert med Proton-kontoer. Ren UX, skjul-min-e-post-aliaser, åpne apper.

protonmail.desc: Kryptert e-post basert i Sveits. Enkel onboarding, kalender/drive-økosystem.
protonmail.why: du bytter fra Gmail for første gang.

tuta.desc: Kryptert e-post og kalender fra Tyskland. Minimal sporingsoverflate.
tuta.why: du vil ha et fokusert personvern-mail-alternativ.

thunderbird.desc: Skrivebords e-postklient med OpenPGP. Bruk med hvilken som helst leverandør — inkludert egen domeneserver.
thunderbird.why: du vil ha klient-side kontroll over e-post.

ddg.desc: Ingen søkehistorikk-profilering for annonser. Enkel bytte fra Google.
ddg.why: du vil ha null friksjon personvern.

bravesearch.desc: Uavhengige indekser eller personvern-proxyer for webresultater uten annonseprofil.

searxng.desc: Self-hostbar metasøk. Aggreger motorer uten å gi ett selskap hele nysgjerrighetsgrafen din.

protondrive.desc: Ende-til-ende-kryptert skylagring. Bedre enn stol-på-oss forbrukerskyer for sensitive dokumenter.
protondrive.why: filer må synces men forbli kryptert.

cryptomator.desc: Klient-side hvelv oppå Dropbox, Google Drive eller hvilken som helst mappe. Krypter før opplasting.
cryptomator.why: du ikke kan forlate nåværende sky ennå.

veracrypt.desc: Åpen kildekode disk- og beholderkryptering for lokale disker og bærbare hvelv. Krypter hele volumer eller lag skjulte volumer.
veracrypt.why: du trenger sterk lokal/offline-kryptering utover skyhvelv.

nextcloud.desc: Self-host filer, bilder og kalendere (Nextcloud) eller P2P-synk uten sentral server (Syncthing).
nextcloud.why: du er klar til å forlate storsky helt.

aegis.desc: Åpen Android 2FA-app med krypterte eksporter. Foretrekk TOTP over SMS.

enteauth.desc: Plattformuavhengig åpen authenticator med valgfri kryptert synk.

yubikey.desc: Phishing-resistent MFA. Bruk sikkerhetsnøkler for e-post, passordbehandler og kritiske kontoer.

graphene.desc: Herdet Android for Pixel. Beste mobile sikkerhets-/personvernposisjon for forbrukere i dag.

lineage_eos.desc: Tilpassede Android-ROM-er for ikke-Pixel-enheter. LineageOS (+ microG) eller /e/OS kutter Google-tjenester; ikke GrapheneOS-nivå herding.
lineage_eos.why: telefonen din ikke er Pixel, men du vil fortsatt ha en de-Googlet ROM.

linux.desc: Forlat Windows-telemetri. Fedora/Debian til daglig bruk; Qubes for seriøs kompartmentering.

ios.desc: Sterk sandkasse ut av boksen. Lockdown Mode, begrens iCloud, skru av annonsesporing, gjennomgå tillatelser.
ios.why: du blir i Apples økosystem med omhu.

organicmaps.desc: Offline-kart basert på OpenStreetMap. Naviger uten å sende posisjon til Google hele tiden.

notes.desc: Krypterte notater med synk på tvers av enheter. Hold dagbøker og utkast utenfor klartekst-skynotater.

blockers.desc: Blokker annonser, sporere og skadelige domener. uBlock på skrivebord; RethinkDNS for mobil.

photos.desc: Kryptert bildesikkerhetskopi (Ente) eller self-hostet Google Photos-alternativ (Immich).

calling.desc: Foretrekk E2EE tale/video. Unngå sensitive samtaler på SMS eller ukrypterte standarder.

cryptpad.desc: Zero-knowledge samarbeidsdokumenter, ark og whiteboards — som Google Docs med E2EE. Self-hostbar.
cryptpad.why: du trenger sanntidssamarbeid uten en Big Tech-kontorpakke.

android_apps.desc: NewPipe: YouTube-frontend uten annonser, sporing eller Google-konto. Aurora Store: installer Play-apper anonymt. Foretrekk F-Droid-bygg.
android_apps.why: du de-Googler Android og fortsatt trenger video eller Play-apper.

privydeck.desc: Vårt personlige personvern-dashbord. Personvernscore, sporingsblokkering på telefon og nettleser med ett trykk, kryptert hvelv (med filrensing og sikker opprydding innebygd), og dataforespørsler — uten Raspberry Pi.
privydeck.why: du vil ha den enkleste alt-i-ett-blokkeren, hvelvet og scoren (start her før du stabler ekstra verktøy).

privbeacon.desc: Personvern-compliance SaaS for nettsteder. Skann sporere og samtykkehull på tvers av 16 lovverk, fiks brudd, og få et verifiserbart Certified Private-merke.
privbeacon.why: du driver nettsted eller app og trenger ekte compliance — ikke en generisk policy-mal.

winprivacy.desc: Forbedre personvern på Windows 10 og 11 med GUI og CLI — kutt telemetri og stram standarder (åpen kildekode, VassDev).
winprivacy.why: du er på Windows og vil ha praktisk herding uten full OS-bytte ennå.

sechardening.desc: Praktiske sikkerhetsherdingsskript for fersk installasjon — et solid utgangspunkt (åpen kildekode, VassDev).
sechardening.why: du setter opp Linux og vil ha en rask, fornuftig baseline.

ublock.desc: Klassisk åpen nettleser-innholdsblokker. Kombiner med Firefox for utmerket annonse- og sporingsfiltrering på skrivebord.
ublock.why: du vil ha et gratis FOSS-tillegg ved siden av eller under PrivyDeck.

rethinkdns.desc: DNS + brannmur-stil beskyttelse for Android. Blokker sporingsdomener systemomfattende utenfor nettleseren.

life.title: Personvern utenom apper
life.lead: Den beste VPN-en fikser ikke overdeling, svake låser eller et kamera mot pulten. Personvern er et livsstilssystem.

1.title: Sosialt og identitet
1.1: Gå gjennom offentlige profiler — fjern fødselsdato, hjemby, arbeidssted, familiebilder.
1.2: Bruk ulike brukernavn per kontekst; slutt å gjenbruke ett handle overalt.
1.3: Skru av ansiktsgjenkjenning og kontaktsynkronisering i sosiale apper.
1.4: Tenk før du poster posisjon i sanntid (vent til du har dratt).
1.5: Lag separate e-postaliaser for shopping, nyhetsbrev og bank.

2.title: Hjem og fysisk
2.1: Dekk til laptop-kamera; foretrekk mikrofoner du kan mute i maskinvare.
2.2: Lås skjermer aggressivt; slå på full diskkryptering overalt.
2.3: Makuler dokumenter med ID-numre — ikke bare resirkuler.
2.4: Vær kritisk til smarthøyttalere i private rom; legg IoT på gjeste-Wi‑Fi.
2.5: Vit hvem som har fysisk tilgang til enhetene dine når du reiser.

3.title: Penger og shopping
3.1: Bruk personvernvennlige betalingsmåter der det er lovlig og praktisk.
3.2: Unngå lojalitetskort knyttet til ekte identitet når det er mulig.
3.3: Ikke fotografer bankkort eller ID inn i sky-kameraruller.
3.4: Meld deg ut av datameglere (varierer per land — gjør årlige runder).
3.5: Hold finansiell 2FA på sikkerhetsnøkler eller authenticator, aldri bare SMS.

4.title: Kommunikasjonsvaner
4.1: Standard til Signal for alt du ikke ville skrevet på et postkort.
4.2: Forsvinnende meldinger for midlertidige planer; skjermbilder finnes fortsatt.
4.4: Ikke diskuter hemmeligheter på arbeidsgiverenheter eller jobbchat.
4.5: Anta at gruppechatter utvider angrepsflaten med hvert nye medlem.

phone.title: Telefonpersonvern — Android og iOS
phone.lead: Telefonen er en sporingssupermaskin du bærer overalt. Lås den ned per plattform.

android.title: Android-herdingsjekkliste
android.note: GrapheneOS-brukere: sandkasse-Google Play er valgfritt — bare hvis du virkelig trenger det.
android.1: Foretrekk moderne Pixel + GrapheneOS om du kan. Ellers hold stock OS oppdatert.
android.2: Installer apper fra pålitelige kilder — Play Store forsiktig, eller F-Droid for FOSS.
android.3: Tillatelsesdiett: nekt posisjon, mic, kamera, kontakter med mindre nødvendig.
android.4: Deaktiver annonse-ID / personlig tilpasning av annonser.
android.5: Skru av unødvendige sensorer: Bluetooth, NFC, nøyaktig posisjon når ledig.
android.7: Låseskjerm: sterk PIN/passordfrase, biometri OK med PIN-fallback.
android.8: Sikkerhetskopi: krypterte kopier du kontrollerer — ikke bare Google One.
android.9: Arbeidsprofil / sekundær bruker for å isolere tvilsomme apper.
android.10: Unngå å sidelaste APK-er fra tilfeldige nettsteder.

ios.title: iOS-herdingsjekkliste
ios.note: iOS er lukket kildekode — kompensér med sterk Apple ID-sikkerhet og minimal appflate.
ios.1: Oppdater iOS raskt — sandkassen er sterk; upatchet er det ikke.
ios.2: Aktiver Lockdown Mode ved målrettede angrep.
ios.3: Personvern og sikkerhet: gå gjennom tillatelser; nullstill sporing.
ios.4: Apple ID: unikt sterkt passord, sikkerhetsnøkkel eller passkeys, Skjul e-posten min.
ios.5: iCloud: vit hva som synces. Avansert databeskyttelse styrker E2EE.
ios.6: Begrens analyse og personlig tilpassede annonser.
ios.7: Safari: aktiver advarsel om svindelnettsteder; vurder Brave/Firefox Focus.
ios.9: USB-tilbehør / beskyttelse mot stjålet enhet ved fysisk trussel.
ios.10: Unngå skumle konfigurasjonsprofiler og MDM du ikke forstår.

desktop.title: PC- og laptop-personvern
desktop.lead: Laptopen holder livsverket ditt. Krypter disken, minimer telemetri, og slutt å behandle nettleseren som en søppeldunk.

windows.1: Bruk lokal konto når mulig; begrens Microsoft-kontosynk.
windows.2: Skru av annonse-ID, skreddersydde opplevelser og full telemetri.
windows.5: Avinstaller bloat; deaktiver oppstartsapper du ikke kjenner.
windows.6: Windows Sandbox / separat nettleserprofil for risikable nettsteder.
windows.7: Vurder Linux når du er klar for renere ark.

macos.1: FileVault på. Brannmur på. Automatiske oppdateringer på.
macos.2: Gå gjennom Personvern og sikkerhet-tillatelser jevnlig.
macos.3: iCloud: Avansert databeskyttelse hvis gjenoppretting passer.
macos.4: Foretrekk App Store eller verifiserte utviklere; Gatekeeper på.
macos.5: Begrens Continuity-funksjoner som kringkaster tilstedeværelse ved behov.
macos.6: Bruk Firefox/Brave; skill jobb og privat browsing.

linux.2: Fedora, Debian eller openSUSE for fornuftige standarder.
linux.3: Flatpak med omhu; foretrekk distropakker for systemverktøy.
linux.5: Qubes OS for sterk appisolasjon (brattere læringskurve).
linux.7: Separat nettleser for bank vs. generell bruk.

u1.title: Krypter eller mist
u1.body: Tapt laptop uten FDE = fullt databrudd. Krypter alltid disker.

u2.title: Passordbehandler overalt
u2.body: Innebygd i nettleser er bedre enn ingenting; Bitwarden/KeePassXC er bedre.

u3.title: Oppdateringer er sikkerhet
u3.body: Upatchet OS/nettleser er den enkleste kompromissveien.

u4.title: Minste privilegium
u4.body: Ikke jobb daglig som admin/root. Ikke installer tilfeldige .exe/.dmg.

u6.title: Offentlig Wi‑Fi = VPN
u6.body: Behandle kafeer og flyplasser som fiendtlige nettverk.

checklist.reset_confirm: Nullstille all sjekklistefremdrift på denne enheten?

principles.title: Personvernprinsipper som aldri går ut på dato

p1.title: Trusselmodell først
p1.body: Beskytt mot risikoene du faktisk har — ikke en filmvillain. Ulike jobber trenger ulike stacker.

p2.title: Minimer data
p2.body: Du kan ikke lekke det du aldri samler. Del mindre, behold mindre, slett det du ikke trenger.

p3.title: Forsvar i dybden
p3.body: Ett verktøy svikter. Lag lag med passord, 2FA, kryptering, oppdateringer og gode vaner.

p4.title: Foretrekk åpent og revidert
p4.body: Åpen kildekode er ikke magi, men hemmelighold er et dårligere bet for sikkerhetskritisk programvare.

p5.title: Brukervennlighet vinner
p5.body: Det private verktøyet du forlater er verre enn det gode nok-verktøyet du bruker daglig.

p6.title: Anta brudd
p6.body: Planlegg gjenoppretting: backups, nøkler du kontrollerer, og kontoer du fortsatt kan ta tilbake.

faq.title: Vanlige spørsmål
faq.a1: Ikke alltid. En VPN skjuler trafikken din for lokale nettverk og ISP, og kan redusere stedbasert sporing — men den gjør deg ikke anonym, og en dårlig VPN er verre enn ingen. Bruk en anerkjent no-logs-leverandør på fiendtlige nett; kombiner med HTTPS, gode nettlesere og kontohygiene.
faq.q2: Er Signal egentlig privat når det krever telefonnummer?
faq.a2: Signal krypterer meldingsinnholdet utmerket. Nummeret er en identifikator for oppdagelse — en tradeoff for brukervennlighet. Hvis det betyr noe for trusselmodellen din, se på Session. For de fleste er Signal fortsatt det beste valget folk faktisk installerer.
faq.q3: Hva er den enkeltendringen med størst effekt?
faq.a3: Passordbehandler + unike passord + authenticator-2FA på e-post. De fleste kontoovertakelser er gjenbrukte passord og SIM-swap, ikke nasjonalstats zero-days.
faq.a4: Hvis du kan, hjelper det mye. Hvis ikke: lås profiler, fjern persondata, stopp sanntidsposisjon, og bruk nettlesercontainere så sporere ikke følger deg overalt.
faq.a5: Ingen analyse, ingen annonsecookies, ingen tredjepartssporere for annonser. Sjekklistefremdrift ligger bare i nettleserens localStorage.
faq.a6: Les prosjektdokumentasjon for verktøyene du tar i bruk. Ressurser som privacyguides.org og offisielle sikkerhetspapirer slår tilfeldige VPN-topplister.
faq.q7: Er PrivGuide bare markedsføring for PrivyDeck og PrivBeacon?
faq.a7: Nei. Guiden eies av samme selskap, noe vi opplyser først. Uavhengige verktøy listes først; Vårt er merket. Interessekonflikter og metode står på Tillit-siden. Opplever du urettferdighet, åpne en GitHub-sak.
faq.q8: Får dere betalt når jeg klikker en app-lenke?
faq.a8: Nei. PrivGuide bruker ikke affiliate-lenker. Krypto-tips er valgfritt og kjøper ikke rangering.

signal.desc: Estándar de oro del mensajero privado. Cifrado de extremo a extremo, mensajes que desaparecen, código abierto, sin anuncios.
signal.why: familia y amigos de verdad lo instalarán.

session.desc: Sin número de teléfono. Resistencia a metadatos por enrutado cebolla. Modelo de anonimato más fuerte.

simplex.desc: Sin teléfono, email ni IDs de usuario persistentes. Enlaces de invitación de un solo uso y relays pensados contra correlación de metadatos. Los datos quedan en el dispositivo.
simplex.why: necesitas máximo anonimato frente a metadatos y correlación.

threema.desc: Mensajería suiza con compra única — sin teléfono ni email. E2EE completa con forward secrecy; apps de código abierto y protocolo auditado.
threema.why: quieres una alternativa de pago con buena jurisdicción, sin modelo de anuncios gratis.

element.desc: Salas E2EE federadas, puentes a otras redes. Puedes autoalojar e infra propia.

firefox.desc: Mejor equilibrio entre usabilidad y control. Combínalo con PrivyDeck y/o uBlock Origin y protección estricta de rastreo.

brave.desc: Basado en Chromium con bloqueo agresivo de anuncios/rastreadores y ventanas privadas con Tor.
brave.why: quieres UX tipo Chrome con mejores defaults.

tor.desc: Tráfico por la red Tor. Esencial para investigación de alto riesgo y eludir censura. No para logins cotidianos.
tor.why: el modelo de amenaza necesita anonimato, no solo privacidad.

mullvad_browser.desc: Tecnología de Tor Browser sin la red Tor — Firefox endurecido anti-fingerprinting.
mullvad_browser.why: lo combinas con una VPN de confianza.

librewolf.desc: Fork endurecido de Firefox sin telemetría y con anti-fingerprinting fuerte por defecto. Excelente navegador diario.
librewolf.why: quieres privacidad de Firefox sin retocar about:config a mano.

mullvad.desc: Cuentas anónimas (sin email), pago en efectivo/cripto, auditado, reputación no-logs.
mullvad.why: te importa más la privacidad que el streaming más rápido.

protonvpn.desc: Buen plan gratuito, apps open source, Secure Core y ecosistema Proton. Ideal para principiantes.

ivpn.desc: Empresa transparente, sin email al registrarse, fuerte anti-rastreo.
ivpn.why: quieres valores tipo Mullvad con más funciones.

bitwarden.desc: Open source, auditado, gratis para individuos. Autoaloja con Vaultwarden si quieres control total.

keepassxc.desc: Base de contraseñas local-first. Controlas archivo, copias y sincronización. Cero dependencia de nube.
keepassxc.why: no quieres vault en la nube de terceros.

protonpass.desc: Integrado con cuentas Proton. UX limpia, alias hide-my-email, apps open source.

protonmail.desc: Correo cifrado con sede en Suiza. Onboarding fácil y ecosistema calendario/drive.

tuta.desc: Correo y calendario cifrados desde Alemania. Superficie de rastreo mínima.
tuta.why: quieres una alternativa de correo enfocada en privacidad.

thunderbird.desc: Cliente de escritorio con OpenPGP. Úsalo con cualquier proveedor, incluido dominio propio.
thunderbird.why: quieres control del correo en el cliente.

ddg.desc: Sin perfilado de historial de búsqueda para anuncios. Cambio simple desde Google.

bravesearch.desc: Índices independientes o proxies de privacidad sin perfil publicitario de consultas.
bravesearch.why: los resultados de DDG no bastan.

searxng.desc: Metabúsqueda autoalojable. Agrega motores sin entregar tu gráfica de curiosidad a una empresa.

protondrive.desc: Almacenamiento en la nube con cifrado E2EE. Mejor que nubes de confianza ciega para documentos sensibles.

cryptomator.desc: Bóvedas del lado del cliente sobre Dropbox, Google Drive o cualquier carpeta. Cifra antes de subir.
cryptomator.why: aún no puedes dejar tu nube actual.

veracrypt.desc: Cifrado de disco y contenedores de código abierto para unidades locales y bóvedas portátiles. Cifra volúmenes enteros o crea volúmenes ocultos.
veracrypt.why: necesitas cifrado local/offline fuerte más allá de bóvedas en la nube.

nextcloud.desc: Autoalojar archivos y calendarios (Nextcloud) o sincronización P2P sin servidor central (Syncthing).
nextcloud.why: estás listo para dejar la gran nube.

aegis.desc: App 2FA open source para Android con exportaciones cifradas. Prefiere TOTP al SMS.

enteauth.desc: Authenticator multiplataforma open source con sync cifrado opcional.

yubikey.desc: MFA resistente al phishing. Llaves para email, gestor de contraseñas y cuentas críticas.
yubikey.why: un robo de cuenta sería devastador.

graphene.desc: Android endurecido para Pixel. Mejor postura de seguridad/privacidad móvil al consumidor hoy.
graphene.why: la seguridad del teléfono es innegociable.

lineage_eos.desc: ROMs Android personalizadas para dispositivos que no son Pixel. LineageOS (+ microG) o /e/OS reducen Google; no alcanzan el nivel GrapheneOS.
lineage_eos.why: tu teléfono no es Pixel pero aún quieres una ROM sin Google.

linux.desc: Deja la telemetría de Windows. Fedora/Debian para el día a día; Qubes para compartimentación seria.
linux.why: la privacidad de escritorio es un objetivo a largo plazo.

ios.desc: Sandbox fuerte de serie. Lockdown Mode, limita iCloud, desactiva ads tracking y revisa permisos.
ios.why: te quedas en el ecosistema Apple con cuidado.

organicmaps.desc: Mapas offline con OpenStreetMap. Navega sin enviar tu ubicación a Google sin cesar.

notes.desc: Notas cifradas con sync multi-dispositivo. Diarios y borradores fuera de notas en texto plano en la nube.
notes.why: Notas de Apple/Google se sienten expuestas.

blockers.desc: Bloquea anuncios, rastreadores y dominios maliciosos. uBlock en escritorio; RethinkDNS en móvil.
blockers.why: el día uno de cualquier viaje de privacidad.

photos.desc: Backup de fotos cifrado (Ente) o alternativa autoalojada a Google Photos (Immich).

calling.desc: Prefiere voz/vídeo E2EE. Evita conversaciones sensibles en SMS o defaults sin cifrar.
calling.why: el contenido de la llamada importa.

cryptpad.desc: Docs, hojas y pizarras colaborativas de conocimiento cero — como Google Docs con E2EE. Autoalojable.
cryptpad.why: necesitas colaboración en tiempo real sin suite ofimática Big Tech.

android_apps.desc: NewPipe: frontend de YouTube sin anuncios, rastreo ni cuenta Google. Aurora Store: instala apps de Play de forma anónima. Prefiere builds de F-Droid.
android_apps.why: estás quitando Google de Android y aún necesitas vídeo o apps de Play.

privydeck.desc: Nuestro panel de privacidad personal. Puntuación de privacidad, bloqueo de rastreadores en móvil y navegador con un toque, bóveda cifrada (con saneado de archivos y limpieza segura integrados) y solicitudes de datos — sin Raspberry Pi.
privydeck.why: quieres el bloqueador, bóveda y puntuación todo-en-uno más simple (empieza aquí).

privbeacon.desc: SaaS de cumplimiento de privacidad para sitios. Escanea rastreadores y huecos de consentimiento en 16 marcos legales y gana el sello Certified Private.
privbeacon.why: gestionas un sitio o app y necesitas cumplimiento real.

winprivacy.desc: Mejora la privacidad en Windows 10 y 11 con GUI y CLI — reduce telemetría (open source, VassDev).
winprivacy.why: estás en Windows y quieres endurecer sin cambiar de SO aún.

sechardening.desc: Scripts prácticos de hardening para una instalación limpia (open source, VassDev).
sechardening.why: montas Linux y quieres una base rápida y sensata.

ublock.desc: El bloqueador clásico de código abierto para el navegador. Combínalo con Firefox en el escritorio.
ublock.why: quieres una extensión FOSS junto a PrivyDeck.

rethinkdns.desc: Protección tipo DNS + firewall en Android. Bloquea dominios de rastreo en todo el sistema.
rethinkdns.why: necesitas bloqueo a nivel de red en apps Android.

1.title: Social e identidad
1.1: Audita perfiles públicos: quita fecha de nacimiento, ciudad, trabajo, fotos de familia.

2.1: Cubre cámaras del portátil; prefiere micrófonos con mute hardware.

2.3: Destruye documentos con números de ID.
2.4: Cuestiona altavoces inteligentes; segmenta IoT en Wi‑Fi de invitados.
2.5: Controla el acceso físico al viajar.

3.1: Usa pagos amigables con la privacidad cuando sea legal y práctico.
3.2: Evita tarjetas de fidelización con tu identidad real si puedes.
3.3: No fotografíes tarjetas ni DNI en la nube.
3.4: Date de baja de data brokers (varía por país).
3.5: 2FA financiero en llaves o authenticator, nunca solo SMS.

4.title: Hábitos de comunicación
4.1: Signal por defecto para lo que no pondrías en una postal.
4.2: Mensajes que desaparecen; las capturas siguen existiendo.
4.3: Verifica números de seguridad con contactos críticos.
4.4: No hables secretos en dispositivos del trabajo.
4.5: Cada miembro nuevo en un grupo amplía la superficie de riesgo.

faq.a1: No siempre. Una VPN oculta tráfico a redes locales e ISP y reduce rastreo por ubicación, pero no te hace anónimo. Una mala VPN es peor que ninguna. Úsala en redes hostiles con un proveedor sin logs de reputación.
faq.q2: ¿Signal es privado si pide mi número?
faq.a2: El contenido está muy bien cifrado. El número es un identificador de descubrimiento. Si eso importa, mira Session. Para la mayoría, Signal sigue siendo la mejor opción que la gente instalará.
faq.q3: ¿Cuál es el cambio de mayor impacto?
faq.a3: Gestor de contraseñas + contraseñas únicas + 2FA con authenticator en el correo.
faq.a4: Si puedes, ayuda mucho. Si no, cierra perfiles, quita datos personales y evita ubicación en tiempo real.
faq.a5: Sin analítica, sin cookies publicitarias, sin rastreadores de terceros. La lista se guarda solo en localStorage.
faq.a6: Documentación oficial de las herramientas y recursos como privacyguides.org.
faq.q7: ¿PrivGuide es solo marketing de PrivyDeck y PrivBeacon?
faq.a7: No. La misma empresa es dueña de la guía — lo declaramos. Las herramientas independientes van primero; Ours están etiquetadas. Detalles en la página Trust.

trust_page.title: Trust & editorial standards
trust_page.lead: We build privacy tools. This guide exists so you are not stuck with only ours. Below: ownership, conflicts, methodology, what this site collects, and how to challenge a listing.

ownership.1: PrivGuide is hosted and owned by Vassbrekke AS, a Norwegian company. The same company builds PrivyDeck, PrivBeacon, and other VassDev tools.
ownership.2: That ownership is a conflict of interest for any listing of our own products. We disclose it everywhere — not only in the footer.
ownership.3: Editorial intent: recommend the best practical tools for each job. When a third-party tool is clearly better for most people, it stays ahead of ours.

roles.1: vassbrekke.no — company identity, legal entity, contact.
roles.2: PrivGuide — how to get private (mostly tools we did not build).
roles.3: PrivyDeck — personal privacy dashboard for individuals.
roles.4: PrivBeacon — website privacy compliance for organizations.

conflicts.1: Products marked Ours are built by Vassbrekke AS / VassDev. They are never unlabeled.
conflicts.2: We do not accept payment for placement, ranking, or a Recommended badge on PrivGuide.
conflicts.3: We do not use affiliate links on PrivGuide. Official website links go to the vendor’s own site.
conflicts.4: Crypto donations support hosting and maintenance. Donors cannot buy a listing or a higher rank.

conflict_rules.1: Ours cards always show an Ours badge and publisher line.
conflict_rules.2: Default app order puts independent tools first; Ours appear after community recommendations (or under the Ours filter).
conflict_rules.3: Ours never outrank a clearly better tool in the same job without a written reason on the card.
conflict_rules.4: Path checklists may mention our products as optional — never as the only option.
conflict_rules.5: If you believe a listing is unfair, open a correction issue — we publish material changes in the changelog.

methodology.1: Recommendations are practical, not maximalist. Usability counts: a private tool you abandon is worse than a good-enough tool you use daily.
methodology.2: We review listings on a rolling schedule. Each card shows a last-reviewed date. Criteria below apply to first-party and third-party tools alike.

criteria.1: Threat-model fit — clear who it protects against, and who it does not.
criteria.2: Security posture — encryption, open source or auditable claims, update cadence, history of incidents.
criteria.3: Privacy business model — how the vendor makes money; avoid predatory free tiers that sell attention.
criteria.4: Jurisdiction & governance — where the org is based and what legal pressure looks like.
criteria.5: Usability — will non-experts actually switch and stick with it?
criteria.6: Official distribution — we link only to official sites or well-known trusted repos (e.g. project GitHub).

transparency.1: PrivGuide is a static site. There is no account system and no advertising.
transparency.2: Checklist progress is stored in your browser’s local storage only. Clearing site data clears progress. Nothing is uploaded to us.
transparency.3: We do not load third-party analytics, ad pixels, or social trackers. Fonts are local/system — not Google Fonts.

collect.1: No cookies for advertising or cross-site tracking.
collect.3: Server access logs (if any) are handled by the host — we do not run a marketing pixel layer on top.
collect.4: Outbound links use rel=noopener noreferrer; we do not append affiliate parameters.
collect.5: Verify with your own blocker — empty network requests beyond the page and assets is the point.

trust_page.title: Trust & editorial standards
trust_page.lead: We build privacy tools. This guide exists so you are not stuck with only ours. Below: ownership, conflicts, methodology, what this site collects, and how to challenge a listing.

ownership.1: PrivGuide is hosted and owned by Vassbrekke AS, a Norwegian company. The same company builds PrivyDeck, PrivBeacon, and other VassDev tools.
ownership.2: That ownership is a conflict of interest for any listing of our own products. We disclose it everywhere — not only in the footer.
ownership.3: Editorial intent: recommend the best practical tools for each job. When a third-party tool is clearly better for most people, it stays ahead of ours.

roles.1: vassbrekke.no — company identity, legal entity, contact.
roles.2: PrivGuide — how to get private (mostly tools we did not build).
roles.3: PrivyDeck — personal privacy dashboard for individuals.
roles.4: PrivBeacon — website privacy compliance for organizations.

conflicts.1: Products marked Ours are built by Vassbrekke AS / VassDev. They are never unlabeled.
conflicts.2: We do not accept payment for placement, ranking, or a Recommended badge on PrivGuide.
conflicts.3: We do not use affiliate links on PrivGuide. Official website links go to the vendor’s own site.
conflicts.4: Crypto donations support hosting and maintenance. Donors cannot buy a listing or a higher rank.

conflict_rules.1: Ours cards always show an Ours badge and publisher line.
conflict_rules.2: Default app order puts independent tools first; Ours appear after community recommendations (or under the Ours filter).
conflict_rules.3: Ours never outrank a clearly better tool in the same job without a written reason on the card.
conflict_rules.4: Path checklists may mention our products as optional — never as the only option.
conflict_rules.5: If you believe a listing is unfair, open a correction issue — we publish material changes in the changelog.

methodology.1: Recommendations are practical, not maximalist. Usability counts: a private tool you abandon is worse than a good-enough tool you use daily.
methodology.2: We review listings on a rolling schedule. Each card shows a last-reviewed date. Criteria below apply to first-party and third-party tools alike.

criteria.1: Threat-model fit — clear who it protects against, and who it does not.
criteria.2: Security posture — encryption, open source or auditable claims, update cadence, history of incidents.
criteria.3: Privacy business model — how the vendor makes money; avoid predatory free tiers that sell attention.
criteria.4: Jurisdiction & governance — where the org is based and what legal pressure looks like.
criteria.5: Usability — will non-experts actually switch and stick with it?
criteria.6: Official distribution — we link only to official sites or well-known trusted repos (e.g. project GitHub).

transparency.1: PrivGuide is a static site. There is no account system and no advertising.
transparency.2: Checklist progress is stored in your browser’s local storage only. Clearing site data clears progress. Nothing is uploaded to us.
transparency.3: We do not load third-party analytics, ad pixels, or social trackers. Fonts are local/system — not Google Fonts.

collect.1: No cookies for advertising or cross-site tracking.
collect.3: Server access logs (if any) are handled by the host — we do not run a marketing pixel layer on top.
collect.4: Outbound links use rel=noopener noreferrer; we do not append affiliate parameters.
collect.5: Verify with your own blocker — empty network requests beyond the page and assets is the point.

tuta.desc: E-mail et calendrier chiffrés d'Allemagne. Surface de pistage minimale.
tuta.why: vous voulez une alternative mail centrée privacy.

thunderbird.desc: Client e-mail bureau avec OpenPGP. Avec tout fournisseur — y compris domaine personnel.
thunderbird.why: vous voulez le contrôle côté client du mail.

ddg.desc: Pas de profilage de l'historique de recherche pour la pub. Changement simple depuis Google.
ddg.why: vous voulez la confidentialité sans friction.

bravesearch.desc: Index indépendants ou proxys privacy sans profil pub autour de vos requêtes.
bravesearch.why: les résultats DDG ne suffisent pas.

searxng.desc: Méta-recherche auto-hébergeable. Agrégez des moteurs sans livrer votre graphe de curiosité.

protondrive.desc: Stockage cloud chiffré de bout en bout. Mieux que les clouds « faites-nous confiance » pour documents sensibles.
protondrive.why: les fichiers doivent se synchroniser chiffrés.

cryptomator.desc: Coffres côté client sur Dropbox, Google Drive ou tout dossier. Chiffrez avant l'envoi.
cryptomator.why: vous ne pouvez pas encore quitter le cloud actuel.

veracrypt.desc: Chiffrement open source de disques et conteneurs pour lecteurs locaux et coffres portables. Volumes entiers ou volumes cachés.
veracrypt.why: vous avez besoin d'un chiffrement local/hors ligne fort au-delà des coffres cloud.

nextcloud.desc: Auto-hébergez fichiers et calendriers (Nextcloud) ou sync P2P sans serveur central (Syncthing).
nextcloud.why: vous êtes prêt à quitter le big cloud.

aegis.desc: App 2FA open source Android avec exports chiffrés. Préférez TOTP au SMS.

enteauth.desc: Authenticator multiplateforme open source avec sync chiffrée optionnelle.
enteauth.why: vous avez besoin de 2FA sur plusieurs appareils.

yubikey.desc: MFA résistant au phishing. Clés pour e-mail, gestionnaire et comptes critiques.
yubikey.why: une prise de compte serait dévastatrice.

graphene.desc: Android renforcé pour Pixel. Meilleure posture sécu/privacy mobile grand public aujourd'hui.
graphene.why: la sécurité du téléphone est non négociable.

lineage_eos.desc: ROM Android custom pour appareils non-Pixel. LineageOS (+ microG) ou /e/OS réduisent Google ; pas au niveau GrapheneOS.
lineage_eos.why: votre téléphone n'est pas un Pixel mais vous voulez quand même une ROM sans Google.

linux.desc: Quittez la télémétrie Windows. Fedora/Debian au quotidien ; Qubes pour une compartimentation sérieuse.
linux.why: la confidentialité bureau est un objectif long terme.

ios.desc: Sandbox fort d'usine. Mode Isolement, limitez iCloud, désactivez le suivi pub, revoyez les permissions.
ios.why: vous restez dans l'écosystème Apple avec prudence.

organicmaps.desc: Cartes hors ligne OpenStreetMap. Naviguez sans diffuser sans cesse votre position à Google.
organicmaps.why: des cartes sans taxe de surveillance.

notes.desc: Notes chiffrées avec sync multi-appareils. Journaux et brouillons hors notes cloud en clair.

blockers.desc: Bloquez pubs, trackers et domaines malveillants. uBlock sur bureau ; RethinkDNS sur mobile.
blockers.why: le jour un de tout parcours privacy.

photos.desc: Sauvegarde photos chiffrée (Ente) ou alternative auto-hébergée à Google Photos (Immich).

calling.desc: Préférez voix/vidéo E2EE. Évitez les conversations sensibles en SMS ou défauts non chiffrés.

cryptpad.desc: Docs, feuilles et tableaux blancs collaboratifs zero-knowledge — comme Google Docs en E2EE. Auto-hébergeable.
cryptpad.why: vous avez besoin de collaboration temps réel sans suite bureautique Big Tech.

android_apps.desc: NewPipe : frontend YouTube sans pubs, tracking ni compte Google. Aurora Store : installer des apps Play anonymement. Préférez les builds F-Droid.
android_apps.why: vous dé-Googlez Android et avez encore besoin de vidéo ou d'apps Play.

privydeck.desc: Notre tableau de bord de confidentialité. Score privacy, blocage des trackers en un tap sur téléphone et navigateur, coffre chiffré (assainissement de fichiers et nettoyage sécurisé intégrés) et demandes d'accès aux données — sans Raspberry Pi.
privydeck.why: vous voulez le bloqueur, coffre et score tout-en-un le plus simple (commencez ici).

privbeacon.desc: SaaS de conformité privacy pour sites. Scanne trackers et manques de consentement sur 16 cadres légaux et délivre Certified Private.
privbeacon.why: vous gérez un site/app et avez besoin d'une vraie conformité.

winprivacy.desc: Renforcez la confidentialité sur Windows 10/11 — GUI et CLI, moins de télémétrie (open source, VassDev).
winprivacy.why: vous êtes sous Windows et voulez durcir sans changer d'OS encore.

sechardening.desc: Scripts pratiques de durcissement pour installation neuve (open source, VassDev).
sechardening.why: vous installez Linux et voulez une base rapide.

ublock.desc: Le bloqueur navigateur open source classique. À coupler avec Firefox sur le bureau.
ublock.why: vous voulez une extension FOSS avec PrivyDeck.

rethinkdns.desc: Protection type DNS + pare-feu pour Android. Bloquez les domaines trackers à l'échelle du système.
rethinkdns.why: vous avez besoin d'un blocage réseau pour les apps Android.

life.title: Vie privée au-delà des apps
life.lead: Le meilleur VPN ne corrige pas le surpartage ni une caméra pointée sur votre bureau.

1.title: Social et identité
1.1: Auditez les profils publics — date de naissance, ville, travail, photos de famille.
1.2: Noms d'utilisateur différents selon le contexte.
1.3: Désactivez la reconnaissance faciale et la synchro des contacts.
1.4: N'affichez pas la position en temps réel.
1.5: Alias e-mail pour achats, newsletters et banque.

2.title: Maison et physique
2.1: Couvrez les caméras ; microphones avec mute matériel.
2.2: Verrouillez les écrans ; chiffrement disque complet partout.
2.3: Détruisez les documents avec numéros d'identité.
2.4: Questionnez les enceintes connectées ; IoT sur Wi‑Fi invité.

3.title: Argent et achats
3.1: Paiements respectueux de la vie privée quand c'est légal et pratique.
3.2: Évitez les cartes de fidélité liées à votre identité réelle.
3.3: Ne photographiez pas cartes/ID dans le cloud.
3.4: Opt-out des data brokers (varie selon le pays).
3.5: 2FA financier sur clé ou authenticator, jamais SMS seul.

4.title: Habitudes de communication
4.1: Signal par défaut pour ce qui ne va pas sur une carte postale.
4.2: Messages éphémères ; les captures existent encore.
4.3: Vérifiez les numéros de sécurité pour les contacts critiques.
4.4: Pas de secrets sur les appareils pro.
4.5: Chaque membre d'un groupe élargit la surface d'attaque.

phone.title: Confidentialité du téléphone — Android et iOS
phone.lead: Votre téléphone est un supercalculateur de pistage. Renforcez-le par plateforme.

android.title: Liste de renforcement Android
android.note: GrapheneOS : Play isolé seulement si vraiment nécessaire.
android.1: Préférez Pixel moderne + GrapheneOS si possible. Sinon, OS à jour.
android.2: Apps depuis sources de confiance — Play Store avec prudence ou F-Droid.
android.3: Régime de permissions : refuser localisation, micro, caméra, contacts sauf besoin.
android.4: Désactiver l'ID pub / personnalisation des pubs.
android.5: Couper Bluetooth, NFC, localisation précise au repos.
android.7: Écran de verrouillage : PIN/phrase fort, biométrie avec secours PIN.
android.9: Profil pro / utilisateur secondaire pour apps douteuses.
android.10: Éviter les APK de sites aléatoires.

ios.title: Liste de renforcement iOS
ios.note: iOS est fermé — compensez par un Apple ID fort et peu d'apps.
ios.2: Mode Isolement face aux attaques ciblées.
ios.3: Revoir chaque permission ; réinitialiser le suivi.
ios.4: Apple ID : mot de passe unique, clé ou passkeys, Masquer mon e-mail.
ios.5: iCloud : savoir ce qui se synchronise ; protection avancée des données.
ios.7: Safari avec alertes fraude ; Brave/Firefox Focus.
ios.8: Transparence du suivi : refuser par défaut.
ios.10: Éviter profils de configuration et MDM obscurs.

desktop.title: Confidentialité bureau et portable
desktop.lead: Chiffrez le disque, minimisez la télémétrie, arrêtez de traiter le navigateur comme une poubelle.

windows.1: Compte local si possible ; limiter la synchro Microsoft.
windows.2: Désactiver ID pub et télémétrie complète.
windows.4: Firefox + uBlock au lieu d'Edge par défaut.
windows.5: Désinstaller le bloat ; démarrages inconnus off.
windows.6: Sandbox / profil navigateur séparé pour sites risqués.
windows.7: Envisager Linux quand vous êtes prêt.

macos.1: FileVault, pare-feu, mises à jour auto.
macos.3: Protection avancée des données iCloud si adapté.
macos.4: App Store / devs vérifiés ; Gatekeeper on.
macos.5: Limiter Continuity si le modèle de menace l'exige.

linux.3: Flatpak avec prudence ; paquets distro pour outils système.
linux.4: Pare-feu et mises à jour sécu auto.

u1.title: Chiffrer ou perdre
u1.body: Portable perdu sans FDE = fuite totale.

u2.title: Gestionnaire partout
u2.body: Bitwarden/KeePassXC valent mieux que le seul navigateur.

u3.body: OS/navigateur non patché = voie facile de compromission.

u4.title: Moindre privilège

u5.title: Sauvegarde hors ligne
u5.body: 3-2-1 avec au moins une copie chiffrée offline.

items.c5: Changer de moteur de recherche hors Google

items.c7: Passer l'e-mail principal à Proton / Tuta (ou le renforcer)
items.c8: VPN sans logs pour voyages et Wi‑Fi public
items.c9: Chiffrement disque complet sur tous les appareils
items.c10: Créer des alias e-mail pour achats et newsletters

items.c12: Auditer vie privée et posts publics des réseaux sociaux

items.c14: Appareils ou profils séparés pour activité à haut risque

p1.body: Protégez-vous des risques réels, pas d'un méchant de film.

p2.title: Minimiser les données
p2.body: On ne fuit pas ce qu'on ne collecte jamais.

p3.title: Défense en profondeur
p3.body: Un outil échoue. Superposez les couches.

p4.title: Préférer ouvert et audité
p4.body: L'open source n'est pas magique, le secret est un pire pari.

p5.title: L'usage gagne
p5.body: L'outil privé abandonné perd face à celui utilisé chaque jour.

faq.title: Questions fréquentes
faq.q1: Ai-je besoin d'un VPN tous les jours ?
faq.a1: Pas toujours. Un VPN masque le trafic aux réseaux locaux et au FAI et peut réduire le pistage de localisation, mais ne vous rend pas anonyme. Un mauvais VPN est pire que rien. Utilisez un fournisseur no-logs réputé sur les réseaux hostiles.
faq.q2: Signal est-il privé s'il demande mon numéro ?
faq.a2: Le contenu est très bien chiffré. Le numéro sert à la découverte — un compromis d'usage. Si c'est un problème, regardez Session. Pour la plupart, Signal reste le meilleur choix réellement adopté.
faq.q3: Quel est le changement à plus fort impact ?
faq.a3: Gestionnaire de mots de passe + mots de passe uniques + 2FA authenticator sur l'e-mail.
faq.a4: Si possible, cela aide beaucoup. Sinon, verrouillez les profils, retirez les données perso, évitez la géoloc en direct.
faq.a5: Pas d'analytics, pas de cookies pub, pas de trackers tiers. La liste reste dans le localStorage uniquement.
faq.a6: Docs officielles des outils et ressources comme privacyguides.org.
faq.q7: PrivGuide n’est-il que du marketing pour PrivyDeck et PrivBeacon ?
faq.a7: Non. La même société possède le guide — nous le disons clairement. Outils indépendants d’abord ; Ours étiquetés. Détails sur la page Trust.

trust_page.title: Trust & editorial standards
trust_page.lead: We build privacy tools. This guide exists so you are not stuck with only ours. Below: ownership, conflicts, methodology, what this site collects, and how to challenge a listing.

ownership.1: PrivGuide is hosted and owned by Vassbrekke AS, a Norwegian company. The same company builds PrivyDeck, PrivBeacon, and other VassDev tools.
ownership.2: That ownership is a conflict of interest for any listing of our own products. We disclose it everywhere — not only in the footer.
ownership.3: Editorial intent: recommend the best practical tools for each job. When a third-party tool is clearly better for most people, it stays ahead of ours.

roles.1: vassbrekke.no — company identity, legal entity, contact.
roles.2: PrivGuide — how to get private (mostly tools we did not build).
roles.3: PrivyDeck — personal privacy dashboard for individuals.
roles.4: PrivBeacon — website privacy compliance for organizations.

conflicts.1: Products marked Ours are built by Vassbrekke AS / VassDev. They are never unlabeled.
conflicts.2: We do not accept payment for placement, ranking, or a Recommended badge on PrivGuide.
conflicts.3: We do not use affiliate links on PrivGuide. Official website links go to the vendor’s own site.
conflicts.4: Crypto donations support hosting and maintenance. Donors cannot buy a listing or a higher rank.

conflict_rules.1: Ours cards always show an Ours badge and publisher line.
conflict_rules.2: Default app order puts independent tools first; Ours appear after community recommendations (or under the Ours filter).
conflict_rules.3: Ours never outrank a clearly better tool in the same job without a written reason on the card.
conflict_rules.4: Path checklists may mention our products as optional — never as the only option.
conflict_rules.5: If you believe a listing is unfair, open a correction issue — we publish material changes in the changelog.

methodology.1: Recommendations are practical, not maximalist. Usability counts: a private tool you abandon is worse than a good-enough tool you use daily.
methodology.2: We review listings on a rolling schedule. Each card shows a last-reviewed date. Criteria below apply to first-party and third-party tools alike.

criteria.1: Threat-model fit — clear who it protects against, and who it does not.
criteria.2: Security posture — encryption, open source or auditable claims, update cadence, history of incidents.
criteria.3: Privacy business model — how the vendor makes money; avoid predatory free tiers that sell attention.
criteria.4: Jurisdiction & governance — where the org is based and what legal pressure looks like.
criteria.5: Usability — will non-experts actually switch and stick with it?
criteria.6: Official distribution — we link only to official sites or well-known trusted repos (e.g. project GitHub).

transparency.1: PrivGuide is a static site. There is no account system and no advertising.
transparency.2: Checklist progress is stored in your browser’s local storage only. Clearing site data clears progress. Nothing is uploaded to us.
transparency.3: We do not load third-party analytics, ad pixels, or social trackers. Fonts are local/system — not Google Fonts.

collect.1: No cookies for advertising or cross-site tracking.
collect.3: Server access logs (if any) are handled by the host — we do not run a marketing pixel layer on top.
collect.4: Outbound links use rel=noopener noreferrer; we do not append affiliate parameters.
collect.5: Verify with your own blocker — empty network requests beyond the page and assets is the point.
